children: New Delhi, Oct. 22 -- Records containing personal information of State Bank of India customers have been found exposed on the dark web, the state-run lender said in a stock exchange filing on Wednesday.

In a preliminary analysis of about 375,000 records, 3,897 with personally identifiable information were identified, the bank said. The leak reportedly includes mobile numbers, dates of birth, names, gender data and addresses, among other details.

The bank was alerted of the breach by its threat intelligence provider, but that's hardly a consolation. That the leak occurred is concerning, especially since it pertains to India's largest bank by several parameters. A full probe is underway, which will reveal the scale of the breach and hopefully its source.

The incident reveals cracks in our data security shield. As digitization levels rise in the country, our cyber defences will need to be fortified, especially now that we risk advanced AI models that can spy vulnerabilities falling into hacker hands.

Data threats have never been more complex and this is exactly why work on AI armoury must be part of India's sovereignty push. Financial sector fortification clearly needs to be one of the top priorities.
